about.title: About {appName}
about.lead: A single place for residents to report disasters to BNPB. Questions are asked one at a time until the report is complete.
about.what.title: What is {appName}
about.card.guided.title: Guided, not a form
about.card.guided.body: Questions are asked one at a time. Most answers only need to be selected.
about.card.ticket.title: With a ticket number
about.card.ticket.body: Every report that is sent gets a ticket number.
about.card.ownWords.title: Numbers from you
about.card.ownWords.body: Numbers are only recorded from your answers. Blank is not counted as zero.
about.steps.title: How to report
about.step1.title: Introduce yourself
about.step1.body: Choose Resident or BPBD Officer, then write your name and number. On the same device, your number is recognized.
about.step2.title: Find the location
about.step2.body: Search for the village, district, or regency/city. Fill in the RT and RW if you know them.
about.step3.title: Choose the type of disaster
about.step3.body: Choose the type of disaster, then its characteristics.
about.step4.title: Tell it through choices
about.step4.body: Answer questions about the order of events: early signs, the main event, the impact, and the current situation. Add a note if needed.
about.step5.title: Fill in the impact and needs
about.step5.body: The number of victims, evacuees, damaged houses and facilities, and urgent needs. Leave blank or choose Don't know if you don't know yet.
about.step6.title: Send the report
about.step6.body: Check the summary, then choose Send. You will receive a ticket number.
about.words.title: Words you can type
about.words.back: kembali: cancels your last answer if you chose wrongly.
about.words.cancel: batal: cancels the report you are filling in, after you confirm it.
about.tips.title: For a complete report
about.do.title: Do
about.do.place: Choose the desa where the incident happened, not the desa where you are now if it is different.
about.do.ownCount: Write the numbers you saw yourself. Write 0 if there are none.
about.avoid.title: Avoid
about.avoid.guess: Guessing the number of victims. Choose Don't know if you are unsure.
about.avoid.false: Making a false report. False reports can lead to legal penalties.
about.limits.title: Usage limits
about.limits: 20 messages per minute, 150 messages per hour, and 300 messages per day per number. 5 reports sent within 24 hours per number. A report you are filling in stays saved when the limit is reached, and you are told what time you can continue.
about.limits.why: These limits protect the service from misuse.

about.emergency.title: Is a life in danger?
about.emergency.body: Do not wait to make a report. Call now.
card.confirm.replaceDraft.title: Create a new report?
card.confirm.replaceDraft.body: The unfinished report ({hazardType}) will be deleted along with all its answers. That report has not been sent and cannot be restored.
card.confirm.declineConsent.title: Do not agree?
card.confirm.declineConsent.body: Without consent, a report cannot be made. The name and number you entered are not saved.
card.confirm.removeProfile.title: Remove {name} from this device?
card.confirm.removeProfile.body: The name and number {maskedNumber} will no longer appear on this device. Any unfinished report from this number will also be cancelled and its contents deleted. Reports already sent are not changed.
card.confirm.cancelDraft.title: Cancel this report?
card.confirm.cancelDraft.body: All answers in this report will be deleted. The report has not been sent and cannot be restored.
card.expired.title: Report has expired
card.expired.body: This report was not changed for 24 hours, so its contents have been deleted and it was not sent. Create a new report if the incident still needs to be reported.
card.placeSearch.title: Location of the incident
card.placeSearch.prompt: Search for the name of the village or kelurahan, district, or regency/city where the incident happened.
card.placeSearch.cut: The list is cut off. Add the name of the district or regency/city to get fewer results.
card.placeSearch.noMatch: No place matches "{query}". Check the spelling, or search for the name of a subdistrict or regency/city and then choose the village.
card.regencyVillages.title: Villages in {areaName}
card.regencyVillages.prompt: Type a village name to filter the list.
card.regencyVillages.cut: The list is cut short. Type a village name to find it.
card.regencyVillages.noMatch: No village in {areaName} matches "{query}". Check the spelling or remove part of the words.
card.neighbourhood.title: RT and RW
card.neighbourhood.prompt: Fill in the RT and RW numbers, or choose Don't know.
card.choice.hazardType.title: Type of disaster
card.choice.hazardType.prompt: What kind of event happened? Choose the closest match.
card.choice.hazardSubtype.title: Characteristics
card.choice.hazardSubtype.prompt: What kind of {hazardType}? Choose Don't know if you are not sure.
card.multiChoice.hint: You may choose more than one.
card.chronologyStep.progress: Story of the event, step {step} of {total}.
card.chronologyReview.title: Timeline put together
card.chronologyReview.prompt: Is there anything you would like to add? For example the name of a river, a road that is blocked, or anything else you saw.
card.chronologyReview.noteHint: Up to 300 characters. Do not write the names of other people.
card.timeCard.title: Time of the event
card.timeCard.prompt: When did the event start? The time uses {zone} time, according to the province of the location.
card.numberForm.prompt: Enter the number. Write 0 if there are none. Leave it empty if you don't know yet, or choose Don't know.
card.numberForm.stillEmpty: Still empty. This information has not been filled in. Fill it in if you know; leave it empty again if you really don't know.
card.textQuestion.hint: Do not write people's names. Up to {max} characters.
card.summary.title: Report summary
card.cancelled.title: Report cancelled
card.cancelled.body: The contents of the report have been deleted. Nothing was sent.
card.sent.title: Report sent
card.sent.body: We have received your report. Our officers will contact you if they need more information. Keep this ticket number.
card.placeSearch.locateHint: The browser will ask for permission to read your location. Or search for a place name below.
card.placeSearch.denied: Location permission was denied. Allow location for this site in your browser, then press Try again.
card.placeSearch.unavailable: Your location could not be read. On a laptop: open System Settings, Privacy and Security, Location Services, then turn it on for this browser. On a phone: turn on GPS. Or search for a place name below.
card.placeSearch.unsupported: This browser cannot read your location. Search for a place name below.
card.placeConfirm.title: Location found
card.placeConfirm.prompt: Check this village or urban ward. The area boundaries on the map are simplified, so make sure it is correct.
card.placeConfirm.nearbyTitle: Choose the village/ward where the incident happened
card.placeConfirm.nearbyPrompt: The villages and wards closest to the point that was read.
card.photos.title: Photos of the incident
card.photos.prompt: Take photos directly with your camera at the scene. Photos are optional, and the report can still be sent without photos.
card.photos.full: You already have {max} photos, the limit for one report. Press Continue.
card.sent.thanks.label: Report sent
card.sent.thanks.title: Thank you, {firstName}!
card.sent.rate.question: How was your experience reporting?
card.sent.heading: Thank you, we have received your report
card.sent.qrHint: Scan this code to open the tracking page on another phone.
card.followUp.title: Add an update for {ticketNumber}
card.followUp.prompt: Choose the parts that have changed, or write the update in the message box, for example "30 people evacuated". The location and time of the incident stay the same.
card.followUp.photosFull: This report already has the maximum number of photos.
card.followUp.keptUntil: This update is saved until {date}, at {time} {zone}.
card.followUp.sent.title: Update sent
card.followUp.sent.body: Your update has been added to report {ticketNumber} as a new version.
card.followUp.cancelled.title: Update cancelled
card.confirm.cancelFollowUp.title: Cancel this update?
card.confirm.cancelFollowUp.body: The update that has not been sent will be deleted. Report {ticketNumber} will not change.
card.confirm.replaceFollowUp.body: The unsent update for {ticketNumber} will be deleted. The report itself will not change.
card.sent.open: Open the report and its documents
card.sent.contact.title: Contact your local BPBD
card.sent.contact.missing: The BPBD number for your area has not been recorded yet.
card.sent.contactPromise: Our officers will contact you if they need more information.
card.sent.numbers.title: Important numbers
card.emergency.type.title: What is happening?
card.emergency.victims.title: Is anyone injured, missing, or trapped?
card.sameEvent.title: The same event?
card.sameEvent.prompt: In Kec. {district} there is already a report of {offers}. Is what you are reporting the same event?
card.sameEvent.yes.tidalWaveAbrasion: Yes, the same tidal waves and abrasion
card.sameEvent.yes.forestFire: Yes, the same forest and land fire
card.sameEvent.yes.buildingFire: Yes, the same fire at the building and residential area
card.sameEvent.yesNote: The type and time are taken from that report; the rest will be asked as usual
card.sameEvent.noNote: Fill in a new report from the start
card.video.title: Video of the incident
card.video.lead: Record directly with the camera, up to 60 seconds and 30 MB each, up to 3 videos. If the signal drops, sending continues from the part that has already arrived.
card.video.broken: Signal lost. {done} of {parts} parts have arrived.
card.video.failed: The video has not been sent. Check your internet connection, then try again.
card.placeSearch.similar: No exact match. These are places with similar spellings.
card.placeSearch.timeout: Your location is taking too long to load. Move to an open area or near a window, then press Use current location again. Or search for a place name below.
card.video.cutOff: The previous video did not finish sending. Choose the same video file to continue from the part that already arrived.
card.sent.nearest.title: Nearest numbers to the report location
card.sent.nearest.source: Numbers are from OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps, measured in a straight line. The numbers may have changed.

chronology.flood.step4.option.roadsBlock: Roads cannot be passed by vehicles
chronology.flood.step4.option.cleanWater: Clean water is muddy or has stopped
chronology.flood.step4.option.phoneSigna: Phone signal is weak or gone
chronology.flood.step4.option.residentsT: Residents are trapped in houses or on roofs

chronology.flood.step5.question: How long has the water been standing at the location?

chronology.flood.step5.option.overHalfDa: The flooding has lasted more than half a day.
chronology.flood.step5.option.overOneDay: The flooding has lasted more than one day.
chronology.flood.step6.question: How is the water now?

chronology.flood.step6.option.stillRisin: At the time of the report, the water was still rising.

chronology.flood.step6.option.startingTo: At the time of the report, the water was starting to recede.
chronology.flood.step6.option.receded.ph: At the time of the report, the water had receded and left mud behind.

chronology.flood.step7.option.powerCable: Power cables are submerged or broken

chronology.landslide.step1.warning: Widening cracks or rumbling from the slope mean the slope may move again. Move away from the slope and from the path below it, do not go back to the house, call 112.
chronology.landslide.step1.option.newCra: New cracks in the ground or house walls
new cracks appeared in the ground or walls
chronology.landslide.step1.option.spring: Spring water turned muddy or suddenly appeared
spring water turned muddy or new seepage appeared
chronology.landslide.step1.option.treesL: Trees, poles, or fences started to lean
trees, poles, or fences started to lean
chronology.landslide.step1.option.rumbli: Rumbling sound from the direction of the slope
a rumbling sound was heard from the slope
chronology.landslide.step2.question: What do you think triggered it?
chronology.landslide.step2.option.heavyR: Heavy rain caused the soil on the slope to become saturated with water and slide
chronology.landslide.step2.option.rainFo: Rain for several days in a row

chronology.landslide.step2.option.earthq: Earthquake shaking caused the slope to slide

chronology.landslide.step2.option.unknow: The soil on the slope slid with a trigger that is not yet known

chronology.landslide.step3.warning: Flows of mud and rocks move fast and travel far. Move sideways away from their path, not straight downhill.
chronology.landslide.step3.option.slowCr: The ground moved slowly down the slope
chronology.landslide.step3.option.sudden: Soil and rocks collapsed suddenly from a cliff
chronology.landslide.step3.option.mudFlo: Flowed like mud mixed with rocks and wood

chronology.landslide.step4.option.riverB: blocked a river or water channel
chronology.landslide.step5.question: How is the slope now?

chronology.landslide.step5.option.stoppe: It has stopped, no new movement

chronology.landslide.step5.option.unknow: The condition of the slope at the time of the report is not yet known.

chronology.landslide.step6.option.onFoot: The access to the location can only be passed on foot.
chronology.landslide.step6.option.cutOff: Cut off, heavy equipment cannot get in yet

chronology.landslide.step7.question: Are there any further hazards nearby?

chronology.landslide.step7.option.riverD: Water is dammed up in the upper river

residents are still below a slope at risk
chronology.landslide.step8.question: Is there anything else you see?

help.title: Help
help.reporting.prepare.q: What do I need to prepare?
help.reporting.prepare.a: Prepare the name of the village or sub-district (kecamatan) where the event happened and the approximate date of the event. The number of victims and the damage can be estimates. If you do not know yet, leave it blank or choose Don't know.
help.reporting.placeRequired.a: A report needs to name the affected village so that it can be checked. The village you choose is recorded together with its sub-district (kecamatan), regency/city, and province.
help.reporting.official.q: Is my report treated as official right away?
help.reporting.official.a: Not yet. A resident report remains a report and does not immediately become official event data. The report is also not shown to the public.
help.reporting.words.a: "kembali" cancels the last answer. "batal" cancels the report you are filling in, after you confirm it.
help.reporting.unsent.q: How long is an unsent report kept?
help.reporting.unsent.a: 24 hours from the last time you filled it in. After that its contents are deleted. Continue the report from the home page.
help.terms.displaced.a: A person who is forced to leave their home because of a disaster, including those evacuated before the impact. They stay temporarily in tents, public buildings, or relatives' homes.
help.terms.familyCard.a: Count per Kartu Keluarga (family card), not per person. One household with one Kartu Keluarga counts as 1 KK, however many members it has.
help.terms.houseDamage.q: Heavily damaged, moderately damaged, lightly damaged, flooded
help.terms.houseDamage.a: Heavily damaged: collapsed, or most of the main structure, walls, and floor are damaged. Moderately damaged: a small part of the structure is damaged but the building is still standing. Lightly damaged: cracks in the plaster, the structure can still be used. Flooded: covered by standing water without structural damage.
help.terms.shakingScale.a: Choose the condition you saw: barely felt, felt without damage, light damage, moderate damage, or heavy damage. The choices follow the BMKG Earthquake Intensity Scale (SIG I to V).
help.status.meaning.q: What does the report status mean?
help.status.meaning.a: A report that has been sent has the status Received and gets a ticket number, for example LA-231126-01. Keep that number.
help.privacy.who.a: Only the BNPB and BPBD officers who handle the report. Your WhatsApp number and photos are not shown to the public. Details are in the privacy policy.
help.privacy.remove.q: How do I remove my number from this device?
help.privacy.remove.a: When choosing the reporter, tap Remove from this device next to your number. A report that is not yet finished is cancelled as well. A report that has already been sent does not change.

help.reporting.emergency.q: How do I report when a life is in danger?
help.reporting.emergency.a: Call 112 first. Then tap Lapor darurat on the home page: it has fewer questions, and the report appears on the officers' desk with an emergency mark. If there are victims, you will be asked whether anyone is trapped and whether anyone needs medical help.
help.reporting.media.q: Can I send photos and videos?
help.reporting.media.a: Yes. Photos are best taken directly at the location. You can send up to 3 videos per report, each video at most 60 seconds long and at most 30 MB. If the signal drops while sending a video, tap Lanjutkan mengirim. Parts that have already arrived are not sent again.
help.reporting.missing.q: How do I report a missing person?
help.reporting.missing.a: Tap Lapor orang hilang on the home page. Search for the village where the person was last seen, then fill in the name, physical features, the time last seen, and a phone number that can be reached. Older photos from your gallery are also allowed. This report is read only by BNPB and the BPBD of that area, and does not appear on the map. One phone number can send 5 missing person reports per day.
help.reporting.language.q: Can I use a regional language?
help.reporting.language.a: Yes. Choose a language at the top of the report page. Parts that have not been translated are still shown in Indonesian. Your answers are recorded as they are.
help.status.missing.q: What do the missing person statuses mean?
help.status.missing.a: Dicari: officers have received the report. Ditemukan selamat or Ditemukan meninggal: officers have received word. Diteruskan ke Basarnas: the search is being handled by the SAR team. The status is shown on the Lapor orang hilang page.
help.status.numbers.a: After the report is sent, the ticket page shows the national emergency numbers: 112 emergency, 117 BNPB, 115 Basarnas, 119 ambulance, 110 police, and 113 fire department.
help.info.outlook.a: The rain forecast and disaster threats for the next three days for the regency or city you search for, with the local BPBD number, 112, and 117.
help.info.warnings.q: How do I get early warnings on my phone?
help.info.warnings.a: In Area info, choose up to 3 districts, the types of disaster, and the level you want to receive, then allow notifications. Warnings for landslides, strong winds, and smoke are labeled Hipotesis because they have not yet been tested against real events. You can stop at any time from the same page.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.draftNote: This is a trial draft. BNPB's legal department will review its contents before the service is opened to the public.
privacy.intro: This policy explains what data the {appName} service collects, what the data is used for, who can see it, and your rights over that data.
privacy.who.title: Who we are
privacy.who.p1: {appName} is a disaster incident reporting service owned by the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB). BNPB is the controller of the personal data you send through this service, in accordance with Law Number 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection and Law Number 24 of 2007 on Disaster Management.
privacy.collected.title: Data we collect
privacy.collected.p1: When you make a report through {appName}, we record:
privacy.collected.item1: Reporter identity: name, WhatsApp number, and role (resident or BPBD officer, along with regency/city and position).
privacy.collected.item2: Report contents: the type and characteristics of the incident, time of the incident, location (GPS point or the village you choose, RT and RW), the number of victims, evacuees, and damage as figures, and needs.
privacy.collected.item3: Photos and videos you send, along with the time and place they were taken.
privacy.collected.item4: Conversations with the AI assistant, the time of messages, and the rating you give for the conversation.
privacy.collected.item5: Early warnings: the subdistrict you choose and your device's notification address, without name, number, or location point.
privacy.collected.p2: We do not ask for the victim's name or Population Identification Number (NIK). Your own name and number, as well as phone numbers, NIK, and email addresses written in messages, are masked before the AI assistant processes them.
privacy.device.title: Data on your device
privacy.device.p1: Some data is stored in your own browser, not on our servers:
privacy.device.item1: Display choices: language and light or dark theme.
privacy.device.item2: Reports without signal: the location point, type of incident, and whether there are victims are stored temporarily on your phone until sent, without name and number.
privacy.device.item4: App files: only public pages and service images, so they can be opened without signal, not the contents of reports.
privacy.device.p2: You can delete them at any time through your browser settings.
privacy.basis.title: Basis for processing
privacy.basis.item1: Consent: you agree when you start a report. Early warnings are requested separately and can be turned off at any time.
privacy.basis.item2: Public service duty: BNPB carries out disaster management in accordance with the law.
privacy.basis.item3: Vital interests: saving lives and helping victims in an emergency.
privacy.use.title: What the data is used for
privacy.use.item1: Compiling disaster incident reports for the BNPB and BPBD officers handling them.
privacy.use.item2: Checking that reports are accurate; officers may contact you if confirmation is needed.
privacy.use.item3: Informing you of the status of your report.
privacy.use.item4: Sending early warnings to the subdistrict you choose.
privacy.use.item5: Showing incidents that are being or have been handled in Alun-alun, without the reporter's identity.
privacy.use.item6: Compiling incident statistics without the reporter's identity for disaster management planning.
privacy.use.p2: Data is not sold and is not used for advertising.
privacy.assistant.title: AI assistant
privacy.assistant.p1: Your messages are processed by the AI assistant to capture the report fields. Only message text that has been masked is sent to the AI service provider; your identity, photos, and coordinates are not sent. The AI assistant does not decide the status of an incident. Officers decide.
privacy.access.title: Who can see it
privacy.access.item1: Officers: only BNPB and BPBD officers who handle incidents in that area can read your report and identity.
privacy.access.item2: Public: reports that are being or have been handled appear in Alun-alun with only the village name, type of incident, and impact figures, without your name, number, photos, or location point.
privacy.access.item3: Link holders: the tracking page is open only to holders of your report's tracking link. Do not share that link.
privacy.others.title: Third-party services
privacy.others.item1: Storage: data is stored in a cloud service managed for BNPB.
privacy.others.item2: Messages: if you report through WhatsApp, messages and report updates go through WhatsApp to your own number.
privacy.others.item3: AI assistant: the language model provider receives message text that has been masked.
privacy.others.item4: Early warnings: sent through your browser's notification service, for example one run by Google, Apple, or Mozilla.
privacy.others.p2: These providers' servers may be outside Indonesia. We only send the data needed for each service.
privacy.storage.title: Storage and security
privacy.storage.p1: Access to data is limited to authorized officers, and each access is recorded. The status history of a report cannot be changed, only added to. Hidden data inside photo files is removed before they are saved. The code in the tracking link is stored in scrambled form.
privacy.retention.title: How long data is kept
privacy.retention.item1: Submitted reports: 2 years after handling is finished, until BNPB sets an official rule.
privacy.retention.item2: Reports not yet submitted: 24 hours from the last time you filled them in, after which the contents are deleted. Reports you cancel are deleted immediately.
privacy.retention.item3: Reports made without a signal on your phone: until they are sent, for at most 14 days.
privacy.retention.item4: Early warnings: until you turn them off, or your browser's notification service no longer recognizes your device.
privacy.rights.title: Your rights
privacy.rights.p1: Under Law Number 27 of 2022, you have the right to:
privacy.rights.item1: Be told what data is used and what it is used for, as on this page.
privacy.rights.item2: See and get a copy of the data we keep about you.
privacy.rights.item3: Correct data that is wrong or incomplete.
privacy.rights.item4: Ask for your identity to be deleted through the 117 call center or persuratan@bnpb.go.id. Numbers on this device can be deleted yourself through Hapus dari perangkat ini. Incident details without personal data are still kept for disaster handling.
privacy.rights.item5: Withdraw your consent: type "berhenti kabar" to stop report updates, or turn off early warnings at any time.
privacy.rights.item6: Object to automated decisions: decisions on reports are always made by officers, not by machines.
privacy.breach.title: If a data breach happens
privacy.breach.p1: If your personal data is leaked or fails to be protected, BNPB will notify you no later than 3 x 24 hours after learning of it, as required by Law Number 27 of 2022, together with the data affected and the steps taken.
privacy.falseReports.title: False reports
privacy.falseReports.p1: Reports that are deliberately untrue get in the way of disaster handling. Reports proven untrue are marked by us as unable to be followed up.
privacy.changes.title: Changes to this policy
privacy.changes.p1: We may update this policy. The effective date is at the top of the page.
privacy.contact.title: Contact
privacy.contact.p1: Have a question or want to use your rights? Contact BNPB through the 117 call center or persuratan@bnpb.go.id.

sigap.home.title: Hello, I'm Sigap
sigap.home.text: Did you see a disaster? Report it here. Your report goes to BNPB and your local BPBD.
sigap.start.title: Hello, I'm Sigap
sigap.start.text: Let's get to know each other. Just a few short details, no account needed.
sigap.feed.title: News from residents
sigap.feed.text: Only reports that officers have followed up on are shown, without the reporter's name.
sigap.info.title: 3-day forecast
sigap.info.text: This is a forecast, not an official warning. Official weather warnings still come from BMKG.
sigap.numbers.title: Save these numbers
sigap.numbers.text: In an emergency, call 112. For follow-up in your area, contact your local BPBD.
sigap.missing.title: Let's search together
sigap.missing.text: Describe the person as clearly as possible and the place where they were last seen. BPBD officers in that area will read it.
sigap.help.title: How to report
sigap.help.text: Just three steps: choose the type of incident, mark the location, answer a few short questions.
sigap.draft.title: I'll help you until the report is complete
sigap.draft.text: Answer one by one. Most only need to be selected.
sigap.sorry.title: We are sorry to hear this
sigap.sorry.text: Put your safety first. If someone needs help right now, call 112.
sigap.tour.label: Pantau Bencana quick tour
sigap.tour.welcome.title: Welcome to Pantau Bencana
sigap.tour.welcome.text: I'm Sigap, a BNPB officer. I will show you how to report a disaster to BNPB and BPBD. This tour takes about 30 seconds.
sigap.tour.emergency.title: Emergency report
sigap.tour.emergency.text: Report a disaster that is happening now and needs a quick response. Just fill in the location, the type of incident, and whether there are victims or not. BNPB and BPBD officers receive it right away.
sigap.tour.report.title: Report an incident
sigap.tour.report.text: Tell us through a chat. I ask questions one by one, and you only need to choose an answer and take photos with the camera.
sigap.tour.missing.title: Report a missing person
sigap.tour.missing.text: Report family or relatives who have not been found. Fill in the name, features, and the place last seen, then the report is sent to officers.
sigap.tour.info.title: Area info
sigap.tour.info.text: Forecasts for rain, floods, landslides, smoke, and wind for the next 3 days, early warnings, and your local BPBD number.
sigap.tour.education.title: Preparedness education
sigap.tour.education.text: What to do before, during, and after a disaster.
sigap.tour.numbers.title: Important numbers
sigap.tour.numbers.text: 112, 117, Basarnas, ambulance, police, and fire department, ready to call.
sigap.tour.language.title: Choose a language
sigap.tour.language.text: This page can be shown in your regional language. Your answer choices reach officers in Indonesian.
sigap.tour.reports.title: My reports
sigap.tour.reports.text: All the reports you have sent and their status are here.
sigap.watch.title: Get ready early
sigap.watch.text: Waspada means be prepared. Follow the instructions of local officials, and stay away from the volcano's danger radius.

Impact figures are ranges drawn from different citizen reports of the same incident, are not added together, and are not official casualty data. Fields the reporter did not fill in are not shown, which does not mean zero. A point on the map marks the center of the village, not the exact location. The reporter's name, number, and photo are never shown.

Type one of these:

• *lapor* to report a disaster
• *darurat* for a short report when the situation is urgent
